prerequisites: General knowledge of English in oral expression, equivalent to B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply knowledge about digital mobile communication techniques and systems, especially those corresponding to the radio interface (CST.2, CG.3).
Interpret the structure of bursts and frames of digital mobile communication systems (CST.2, CG.3).
Measure, simulate, and characterize the radio channel (CST.2, CG.4, CG.5).
Use measurement and characterization procedures and techniques for mobile communication systems and the communication elements used (CST.2, CG.5).
Plan mobile communication systems (CST.2, CG.3, CG.5, CG.6).
Identify standardization bodies and information sources related to mobile and, in general, wireless communication technologies (CST.2, CG.6).
Synthesize information on emerging or standardizing technologies in the field of mobile communications (CST.2, CG.3, CG.6).
Read, draft, and produce documentation in English on a scientific-technical topic within the field of study (CST.2, CG.4, CG.6, CG.9).
Give a presentation in English of a scientific-technical work within the field of study (CST.2, CG.4, CG.9).

syllabus_topics: Cellular systems and their evolution (from 1G to 6G perspectives) in terms of capacity, coverage, cost, performance and technologies used.
Long Term Evolution (LTE) and LTE advanced: Characteristics; Network architecture; Radio interface.
4G system planning. Link budgets. Basic concepts of network management and operation. Technologies and equipment involved in deployment and operation at system and subsystem level.
Personal area networks (Bluetooth, IEEE802.15) and body area networks. WPANs and WBANs
Metropolitan area networks (WiMAX, Mobile WiMAX, IEEE802.16d/e). WMANs

Advancement over previous generations. Key operational and performance indicators (KPIs). Applications and use cases. Characteristics, standardization, and evolution. Network architecture. Radio interface. 5G system planning. Link budgets. Basic concepts of network management and operation. Technologies and equipment involved in deployment and operation at system and subsystem level.
6G perspectives. Objectives and KPIs (Key performance indicators) being proposed. Enabling technologies. IoE (Internet of everything).
Particularities and operation. Types of orbits used. Mobile satellite communication systems. Commercial system constellations. Terminals.

assessment_methods.method: Classroom Practical Work (PA) - Oral presentation in English

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final theoretical grade is 1xT1. The final practical grade is calculated as (0.25 x P1) + (0.17 x P2) + (0.08 x P3) + (0.17 x P4) + (0.33 x PA). The final grade is 40% Theoretical + 60% Practical. To pass, the sum of theoretical and practical grades must be 5 or higher. For the extraordinary assessment, students can choose to keep their ordinary practical grade or take a new practical exam (PL). The final grade is 55% Theoretical + 45% Practical. To pass, the sum of theoretical and practical grades must be 5 or higher.
